answer: A collateralized staking protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock bonds at its network vertex before executing tasks. An attacker incurs linear capital costs per identity, locking up scarce liquidity that forfeits staking nectar and risks slashing during misbehavior. Validators pass interaction graphs through an analytical prism to isolate correlated clusters. However, this design penalizes undercapitalized agents and fails against adversaries with massive treasury reserves.
